title: Meter Shop Billing Adjustment Worksheet — Meter Error Refund on Electric Service by Rate Schedule Accounts
content:
**Rule of the worksheet.** A member-requested meter test that finds the meter of an Electric Service by Rate Schedule account fast beyond the schedule's accuracy tolerance is settled by a meter error refund on the same service account. The refund is figured from the latest test on the account found fast and the registration error that test found (the meter error percent, stated as a positive percent when the meter runs fast).

1. **Rebill window.** The rebill window runs back the schedule's maximum number of corrected billing periods, in whole months, from the current date, so that it covers the energy charge lines dated less than that many whole months before the current date. The maximum is the schedule's own figure on the meter test terms table.
2. **Energy of the window.** The amounts of the energy charge lines of the service account dated in the rebill window, added together.
3. **Overbilled share.** The error percent divided by one hundred plus the error percent.
4. **Meter error refund.** The energy of the window multiplied by the overbilled share, rounded to the cent. It is posted as one bill credit with the reason meter error refund, whose source is the meter test.

The share itself is carried unrounded; only the refund is rounded to the cent.

### Worked examples (hypothetical Schedule R accounts; six-period window from the meter test terms table)

| Error found | Overbilled share | Energy charge lines of the window | Meter error refund |
|---|---|---|---|
| 4.00 percent fast | 4 divided by 104 | $780.00 | $30.00 |
| 2.50 percent fast | 2.5 divided by 102.5 | $1,212.40 | $29.57 |
| 10.00 percent fast | 10 divided by 110 | $660.00 | $60.00 |

Second row in words: $1,212.40 multiplied by 2.5 is $3,031.00; divided by 102.5 that is $29.5707, which rounds to $29.57.

### Points of judgement

- The figures come from the latest test found fast; an earlier fast test on the account is not the one settled.
- Only energy charge lines enter the energy of the window: facility, demand, power cost adjustment, sales tax and minimum lines do not.
- The window is counted back from the current date, not from the date of the test.
